plan: FICTIONAL EVALUATION FIXTURE. I'm opening a small bakery in a rented storefront in three months. I'm funding it from my savings and will hire two part-time staff.

experts.objective: Whether the funding covers setup and the early months of trading.
Licences and regulations for opening a food business.
questions: What matters most for legal & regulatory?

experts.objective: Whether staffing and premises support the planned opening.
questions: What matters most for operations & logistics?

findings.title: Savings runway before revenue is steady
findings.observation: Depending on the savings available and monthly fixed costs, there may be little buffer if early sales are slow.
findings.why_it_matters: Running out of cash in the first months could force the bakery to close.
assumptions: Early revenue will not cover fixed costs straight away

findings.title: Equipment costs may exceed the setup budget
findings.observation: If the storefront needs commercial ovens or refrigeration that are not already installed, setup costs could be higher than expected.
findings.why_it_matters: A larger setup spend reduces the cash buffer for trading.
assumptions: The storefront is not already equipped as a bakery

assignment.objective: Whether the funding covers setup and the early months of trading.

findings.title: Two part-time staff may not cover opening hours
findings.observation: Depending on the planned opening hours, two part-time staff plus the owner may leave some shifts short.
findings.why_it_matters: Short-staffed shifts could limit opening hours or lead to burnout.
assumptions: The bakery will open most days of the week

findings.title: Lease terms may limit fit-out work
findings.observation: If the lease restricts alterations, installing baking equipment or ventilation may need landlord approval.
findings.why_it_matters: Approval delays could push back the opening date.
assumptions: The fit-out needs structural or ventilation changes
